The test and type-only changes are clean based on the provided evidence.","fileVerdicts":[{"path":"apps/web/test/lib/getSchedule.test.ts","verdict":"clean"},{"path":"packages/lib/slots.ts","verdict":"clean"},{"path":"packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts","verdict":"issues"},{"path":"packages/types/schedule.d.ts","verdict":"clean"}],"findings":[{"title":"Availability check rejects slots that merely start inside working hours","claim":"The new working-hours guard computes `end` from `slotStartTime` instead of the slot's actual end (`slotEndTime`). As a result, any slot whose start minute is within a working-hours window is treated as valid even if the meeting duration extends past `workingHour.endTime`. For example, a 60-minute event starting at 16:30 in a 09:00-17:00 window will pass because both `start` and `end` are set to 16:30. This introduces bookable slots that overflow the organizer's configured working hours.","path":"packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts","startLine":131,"endLine":136},{"title":"Date overrides are applied to the wrong users during selected-slot filtering","claim":"In the selected-slots filtering branch, `checkIfIsAvailable` is called with only `busy`, `eventLength`, and `currentSeats`; it no longer receives the candidate user's `dateOverrides` or `workingHours`. Because `checkIfIsAvailable` now defaults those to empty arrays and returns `true` before the busy check when a matching date override exists, this branch can keep a user available even when their normal hours or date override should exclude the slot. That means reserved-slot reconciliation can reintroduce slots outside a host's actual availability.","path":"packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts","startLine":579,"endLine":585},{"title":"Zero-length date overrides are never recognized because Dayjs objects are compared by reference","claim":"The new date-override logic tries to detect an all-day/zero-length override with `dayjs(date.start)... === dayjs(date.end)...`, but `===` compares object identity, not timestamp equality. This condition is therefore always false for distinct Dayjs instances, so zero-length overrides are never handled by the intended branch. The subsequent range checks then treat such overrides as excluding every slot on that day, which is a concrete behavior change from the intended special-case handling.","path":"packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots.ts","startLine":108,"endLine":109}]}

findings.claim: In the selected-slots filtering branch, `checkIfIsAvailable` is called with only `busy`, `eventLength`, and `currentSeats`; it no longer receives the candidate user's `dateOverrides` or `workingHours`. Because `checkIfIsAvailable` now defaults those to empty arrays and returns `true` before the busy check when a matching date override exists, this branch can keep a user available even when their normal hours or date override should exclude the slot. That means reserved-slot reconciliation can reintroduce slots outside a host's actual availability.
findings.title: Date overrides are applied to the wrong users during selected-slot filtering
